questions.knowledgeNote: r = 2, |r| > 1: partial sums 2^n-1 diverge, no sum.
questions.question: Q1(a). Does 1+2+2^2+2^3+... have a sum?
questions.solution: r = 2 with |r| > 1: the partial sums S_n = 2^n-1 grow without bound, so the series has no sum.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.2 Q1(a); book p220 = PDF p247 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: r = -1 oscillates between 1 and 0: no limit, no sum.
questions.question: Q1(b). Does 1+(-1)+1+(-1)+... have a sum?
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.2 Q1(b); book p220 = PDF p247 (vision read)
questions.solution: r = -1: partial sums alternate 1, 0, 1, 0, ... with no limit, so the series has no sum.

questions.knowledgeNote: r = 1/3: S = 1/(2/3) = 3/2, but the question only asks existence.
questions.question: Q1(c). Does 1+1/3+1/3^2+1/3^3+... have a sum?
questions.solution: r = 1/3 with |r| < 1: the series converges (its sum is 1/(1-1/3) = 3/2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.2 Q1(c); book p220 = PDF p247 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(d). Does 3+3/2+3/4+3/8+... have a sum?
questions.solution: r = 1/2 with |r| < 1: the series converges (its sum is 3/(1-1/2) = 6).

questions.question: Q1(e). Does 0.6+0.06+0.006+... have a sum?
questions.solution: r = 1/10 with |r| < 1: the series converges (its sum is 0.6/(1-1/10) = 2/3). Existence key (c), (d), (e) matches the printed Answers, p221.

questions.question: Q2(a). Find the sum of 16+8+4+2+...
questions.solution: a = 16, r = 1/2 (|r| < 1, so the sum exists). S = a/(1-r) = 16/(1/2) = 32 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.2 Q2(a); book p221 = PDF p248 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(b). Find the sum of 5+5/2+5/4+5/8+...

questions.question: Q3. The sum to infinity of a geometric series is 15, and the first term is 3. Find the common ratio.
questions.solution: 3/(1-r) = 15, so 1-r = 3/15 = 1/5, giving r = 4/5 (matches the printed key; |r| < 1 so the sum is valid).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.2 Q3; book p221 = PDF p248 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: The exponents 1/3+1/9+... sum to 1/2, so the product is 3^(1/2).
questions.question: Q5. Prove that 3^(1/3)·3^(1/9)·3^(1/27)·... = √3.
questions.solution: The product equals 3^(1/3+1/9+1/27+...). The exponent is a geometric series with a = 1/3, r = 1/3: sum = (1/3)/(1-1/3) = 1/2. So the product is 3^(1/2) = √3.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.2 Q5; book p221 = PDF p248 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: y > 0 gives 0 < x < 1, so x/(1-x) applies; x = 1/(1+y) turns 1-x into y/(1+y).
questions.question: Q6. If x = 1/(1+y) with y > 0, prove that x+x^2+x^3+... to infinity = 1/y.
questions.solution: Since y > 0, 0 < x = 1/(1+y) < 1, so the infinite sum is x/(1-x). Now 1-x = 1-1/(1+y) = y/(1+y) = xy, so x/(1-x) = x/(xy) = 1/y.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.2 Q6; book p221 = PDF p248 (vision read)
